title: beta-elemene, a sesquiterpene constituent from Curcuma phaeocaulis inhibits the development of endometriosis by inducing ferroptosis via the MAPK and STAT3 signaling pathways.
authors: Fu, Zhiyi; Liu, Hao; Kuang, Yanqi; Yang, Jiumei; Luo, Meicheng; Cao, Lixing; Zheng, Weilin
one_liner_zh: 该文研究β-榄香烯通过MAPK/STAT3通路诱导铁死亡治疗子宫内膜异位症，仅涉及分子对接，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: The rhizome of Curcuma phaeocaulis Valeton, Curcuma wenyujin Y.H. Chen & C. Ling, or Curcuma kwangsiensis S. G. Lee et C. F. Liang, commonly known as Wen-E-Zhu and E'zhu, has been utilized in traditional Chinese medicine for the treatment of cancer and gynecological diseases since antiquity. This traditional medicinal herb is highly esteemed for its efficacy in promoting blood circulation, dissolving blood stasis, reducing swelling, and alleviating pain. beta-Elemene (beta-ELE), a sesquiterpene compound derived from Curcuma phaeocaulis, has demonstrated potential in inhibiting tumor cell proliferation and inducing ferroptosis, which have been extensively studied in various malignant neoplasms. Previous studies have confirmed that Sparganium stoloniferum-Curcuma phaeocaulis containing beta-ELE may possess anti-endometriotic properties. However, the exact mechanism underlying beta-ELE's anti-endometriosis activity remains largely unknown and requires further research and investigation. AIM OF THE STUDY: To identify the anti-endometriosis target of beta-ELE and elucidate the underlying molecular mechanism of beta-ELE in endometriosis, focusing on inducing ferroptosis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The target pathway of beta-ELE in endometriosis treatment was predicted through network pharmacology and bioinformatics analysis. Surface plasmon resonance-high performance liquid chromatography-protein mass spectrometry (SPR-HPLC-MS) and molecular docking were used to further identify the potential targets of beta-ELE in endometriosis. The immortalized endometriosis epithelial cell line 12Z was used for in vitro study. The effect of beta-ELE on cell proliferation and migration was detected by CCK-8, EdU and wound healing assay, and ultrastructural changes were examined via transmission electron microscopy. The effect of beta-ELE-induced ferroptosis was determined by western blot, immunohistochemistry staining and flow cytometry. SPR affinity analysis was performed to specific the direct interaction between beta-ELE and FTH1, FTL, GPX4, STAT3 and MAPK14. To establish a mouse model of endometriosis and to assess the inhibitory effects of beta-ELE and ELE injection on endometriosis in vivo as well as safety profile of administration, and investigate the effects and underlying mechanisms of beta-ELE and ELE injection on ferroptosis in ectopic lesions. RESULTS: SPR-HPLC-MS was employed to identify 76 potential targets of beta-ELE for endometriosis treatment, closely linked to ferroptosis. Molecular docking revealed that glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), ferritin heavy chain 1 (FTH1), ferritin light chain (FTL), signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3), and mitogen-activated protein kinase 14 (MAPK14) are key action targets of beta-ELE in endometriosis. Further investigations revealed that beta-ELE inhibited the proliferation and migration of endometriotic cells in vitro while inducing ferroptosis, as evidenced by increased levels of iron, reactive oxygen species (ROS), and lipid peroxidation. In a mouse model, beta-ELE inhibited the growth of endometriotic lesions, induced ferroptosis, suppressed fibrosis, and exhibited anti-endometriotic effects. Mechanistically, beta-ELE downregulates the expression levels of GPX4, FTH1, and FTL and inhibited the phosphorylation of STAT3 and MAPK14, which may elucidate its underlying molecular mechanisms. CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that the inhibitory effect of beta-ELE on endometriosis by inducing ferroptosis in vitro and in vivo. Our results revealed that beta-ELE exerts anti-endometriosis effects by inducing ferroptosis via the MAPK and STAT3 signaling pathways.
abstract_zh:
民族药理学相关性：莪术（Curcuma phaeocaulis Valeton）、温郁金（Curcuma wenyujin Y.H. Chen & C. Ling）或广西莪术（Curcuma kwangsiensis S. G. Lee et C. F. Liang）的根茎，通常称为温莪术和莪术，自古以来在传统中医中被用于治疗癌症和妇科疾病。这种传统草药因其在促进血液循环、消散血瘀、减轻肿胀和缓解疼痛方面的功效而备受推崇。β-榄香烯（beta-ELE），一种源自莪术的倍半萜类化合物，已显示出抑制肿瘤细胞增殖和诱导铁死亡（ferroptosis）的潜力，这些作用已在多种恶性肿瘤中得到广泛研究。先前的研究已证实，含有beta-ELE的三棱-莪术可能具有抗子宫内膜异位症的特性。然而，beta-ELE抗子宫内膜异位症活性的确切机制仍 largely 未知，需要进一步研究和探讨。

研究目的：识别beta-ELE的抗子宫内膜异位症靶点，并阐明beta-ELE在子宫内膜异位症中的潜在分子机制，重点关注诱导铁死亡。

材料与方法：通过网络药理学和生物信息学分析预测beta-ELE在子宫内膜异位症治疗中的靶向通路。使用表面等离子体共振-高效液相色谱-蛋白质质谱联用（SPR-HPLC-MS）和分子对接进一步识别beta-ELE在子宫内膜异位症中的潜在靶点。永生化子宫内膜异位症上皮细胞系12Z用于体外研究。通过CCK-8、EdU和伤口愈合实验检测beta-ELE对细胞增殖和迁移的影响，并通过透射电子显微镜检查超微结构变化。通过蛋白质印迹、免疫组织化学染色和流式细胞术确定beta-ELE诱导铁死亡的效果。通过SPR亲和力分析明确beta-ELE与FTH1、FTL、GPX4、STAT3和MAPK14之间的直接相互作用。建立小鼠子宫内膜异位症模型，评估beta-ELE和ELE注射剂在体内对子宫内膜异位症的抑制效果及给药安全性，并研究beta-ELE和ELE注射剂对异位病灶中铁死亡的影响及其潜在机制。

结果：采用SPR-HPLC-MS识别了beta-ELE用于子宫内膜异位症治疗的76个潜在靶点，这些靶点与铁死亡密切相关。分子对接显示，谷胱甘肽过氧化物酶4（GPX4）、铁蛋白重链1（FTH1）、铁蛋白轻链（FTL）、信号转导和转录激活因子3（STAT3）以及丝裂原活化蛋白激酶14（MAPK14）是beta-ELE在子宫内膜异位症中的关键作用靶点。进一步研究表明，beta-ELE在体外抑制子宫内膜异位症细胞的增殖和迁移，同时诱导铁死亡，表现为铁、活性氧（ROS）和脂质过氧化水平升高。在小鼠模型中，beta-ELE抑制了子宫内膜异位症病灶的生长，诱导铁死亡，抑制纤维化，并表现出抗子宫内膜异位症效果。机制上，beta-ELE下调GPX4、FTH1和FTL的表达水平，并抑制STAT3和MAPK14的磷酸化，这可能阐明其潜在的分子机制。

结论：本研究证明beta-ELE通过在体外和体内诱导铁死亡来抑制子宫内膜异位症。我们的结果表明，beta-ELE通过MAPK和STAT3信号通路诱导铁死亡，从而发挥抗子宫内膜异位症作用。
